The Templeof Mercury

Heart of the Temple, Mercury its Hinge, and all its Offices, co-conspirators in the Work: I bring you my whole self: my Voice, and my Joy, Will, and Intent. Deed into word. By my Birthright, the Door is open.

A practice kept in a notebook, by hand, between those words and their closing.

Five books. The first is the whole of it; the rest are the things you keep near your hand. Nothing here is required reading, and the practice begins with a pen and one honest page.

The Book of the Temple of Mercury

The whole thing. The practice, the Mercurian, the Temple and its nineteen, the working, the Way of Ma’at, and how to keep and adapt it.

Start here. Part One alone is enough to begin tonight.

The Model Book

A notebook shown fully set up: the Door inside the covers, the Dedication on the first page, the rites close at hand, and the Ledger ruled at the back.

Open beside a blank notebook when you are making your own.

The Mercurial Psalter

Ten hymns, six collects, nine prayers for convening a body of the Temple, an antiphon for each Office, a litany, and five blessings.

For saying aloud. A prayer read silently is a paragraph.

A Mercurial Almanac for 2027

Every day of the Calendar set against one particular sky: the fixed feasts, and Mercury’s own cycle from the ephemeris, turn by turn.

Keep it near the Book and mark the five days you will actually keep.

Dyadic Neo-Enochian

A companion on the system the Temple grew from: the four dyads, the Great Table, grafting, the derivation of names, and four complete workings.

Never required. For the Scribe who wants to know where the five names of the Heart came from.
